localObjective.condition: Given an incline angle beta and friction coefficient mu
localObjective.criterion: classify equilibrium or slip by comparing beta with phi = arctan(mu) and locating the resultant reaction relative to the friction cone

gapDecision.currentCoverage: Chapter prose defines the cone and canonical Sim2 exposes the boundary, but a focused mount is needed to isolate the compare-and-classify objective.
gapDecision.modalityRationale: The mounted canonical simulation provides immediate state change across the beta equals phi boundary without duplicating the formula.
gapDecision.misconceptionTarget: Friction always equals mu times N, even when the body remains below the limiting state.
gapDecision.evidenceTarget: Learner predicts the threshold, changes beta or mu, and explains the state using beta compared with phi.

script: Set beta to 18 degrees and mu to 0.45.
Read phi from arctan(mu) and identify equilibrium.
Increase beta through phi and observe the state label change.
Increase mu and explain why the cone widens.

storyboard.narrativePurpose: Connect material friction to admissible reaction direction

math.expression: tan(phi) = mu; slip iff beta > phi
math.units: beta and phi are in degrees; mu is dimensionless.
assumptions: Rigid block on a planar incline
The two-dimensional section represents the friction cone around the contact normal

accessibility.keyboard: Both native sliders and the Sim2 drag handle support keyboard input.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Sim2 starts without playback and suppresses the handle pulse when reduced motion is requested.
accessibility.textAlternative: The static diagram and formula example state cone angle, incline angle, and equilibrium result without relying on color.

captions.reason: The asset has no audio or timed dialogue.

review.claim: Pilot artifact only. No learner outcome or institutional acceptance claim is made.
